Israeli Election Deadlock
Exit polls suggest
no clear winner
in Israel's first election since the Hamas-led Oct. 7 attacks and the war in Gaza, likely setting the stage for weeks of negotiations.
Israelis turned out in
record numbers
for an election widely seen as a referendum on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s nearly uninterrupted 17-year rule, amid wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran. Neither Netanyahu's nationalist-populist coalition nor a centrist coalition led by his former military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot appears to have secured a parliamentary majority.
Arab-led parties emerged
as the next largest bloc. Both Netanyahu and Eisenkot's coalitions have previously refused to partner with them but may need to reconsider to secure a governing
majority.
Israelis vote for parties rather than individual candidates. A party leader must build a majority
coalition to become prime minister. Learn how Israeli elections work
here
(w/video).

Humanitarian Ceasefire Begins
Russia and Ukraine began a
localized ceasefire
yesterday in Russian-occupied Oleshky, allowing aid and evacuations for roughly 2,000 residents facing dwindling supplies. The White House credited first lady Melania Trump with brokering the agreement, which is expected to last through at least Saturday.
Oleshky, located along the Dnipro River in southern Ukraine's Kherson region, fell to Russian forces in February 2022 and was devastated by flooding following a
dam collapse
in 2023. The river separates Russian and Ukrainian forces, and land mines and drone attacks have made escaping dangerous. The area has
received no food
by road since late May, according to UN human rights groups. Aid workers plan to deliver food, water, and medicine before opening evacuation routes.
The agreement marks an expanded diplomatic role for the first lady, who previously helped
reunite 34 children
with their families and used contacts established through those efforts to negotiate the ceasefire.
Your Loyalty Could Be Costing You
You can't control inflation or what you pay at the gas pump. But one driving expense you can do something about? Your car insurance.
Car insurance is
one of those things
that's not on everyone's mind too often. The problem with setting it and forgetting it, though? Some insurers
quietly raise premiums
over time even for long-term customers—meaning you could be paying more
just for being loyal

Tennessee Prison Break
A multistate manhunt is underway for a
convicted murderer
who escaped from a Tennessee prison late Sunday. Security footage allegedly shows 28-year-old Jacob Allen Morley stealing a truck from a nearby farm;
watch here
Morley was convicted of first-degree murder for killing his coworker Cody Birchfield in 2022. The two worked at a pallet manufacturing company before Birchfield’s body was discovered in a metal box under Morley’s house; forensic analysis suggests he was killed by a gunshot wound to the head. Before Sunday, Morley’s supervision level at the prison was listed as “low.” The incident marks the latest escape by a Tennessee inmate in recent weeks; a 69-year-old prisoner convicted of robbery fled
a Nashville hospital
earlier this month but was quickly recaptured.
There are
hundreds of prison breaks
per year in the US. Many involve low-risk inmates, with an estimated one-fifth of incidents involving violence—most likely at the time of escape.
